continuation.name: crux (attempt 1, resumed continuation)
continuation.result: did not independently solve; mechanism fully re-derived and verified
continuation.what_it_established: flag = pkcs7_unpad(AES-256-CBC-dec(fixed 64B CT, SHA256(M), IV)); M = canonical Pratt cert of the 256-bit prime N; proved full deterministic branch coverage of the 3270 decode; validated the formula byte-exact vs the wasm on multiple inputs.
continuation.why_it_stalled: Encoded the prime-2 leaf as a non-canonical 14-byte 0x01-node (key=2, empty value) instead of the canonical single 0x00 byte. The verifier accepts both, so the cert passed and reached the final AES, but hashed to the wrong SHA-256 key. This produced a phantom '216 free leaf-value bytes' and a fruitless SHA-256 preimage hunt: a validated SHA-NI brute over the full uniform 4-byte space, ~50 deterministic value conventions, modexp-residue analysis, and full state-coverage instrumentation.
continuation.resolution: Reading the attempt-2 write-up revealed the 0x00-leaf grammar. Rebuilding with 0x00 leaves gives the exact 3891-byte cert / 5208-char input; the unmodified main.wasm returns the flag, reproduced byte-for-byte in this session.
